source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:math/0410354v3, 13 January 2006; corroborates the cited 2005 journal article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies pointwise random-design regression at a degenerate point and gives regularly-varying-design pointwise minimax rates.

The article estimates a regression function at one fixed point under potentially vanishing or exploding design density, using a Lepski-type local-polynomial selector adaptive to local design and smoothness.
The paper studies random-design uniform estimation with a spatially dependent normalization for density-vanishing locations and constructs a design- and smoothness-adaptive estimator.
The paper treats known univariate design densities with finitely many well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros, global L2 minimax risk, and adaptive wavelet estimation.
The location-based paper defines the BATEC on a bivariate assignment boundary and assumes a continuous score density bounded away from zero on compact support for its main sharp-DGP theory.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–3, especially equations (1)–(2) and discussion of Theorems 4–6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies pointwise and uniform BATEC estimation and inference using isotropic distance-based local-polynomial procedures, including a minimax lower bound for that estimator class.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make every side average total by specifying a deterministic zero-count value, clipping it to the trace envelope, and include its fallback-event contribution in the oracle-risk bound.

Replace “one canonical point per induced cell” with an explicit ordered selector, such as the lexicographically least endpoint/intersection or rational-grid representative, and prove its measurable dependence on the first-half sample.

Add a short corollary comparing the flat-strip estimator directly with the parent count-qualified rule, isolating precisely the severity-layer argument that removes the isolated-regime global logarithm.

recommended_next_step: Repair the two total-measurability defects in the estimator construction, then advance this field-tier novelty kernel to Stage 0.
